pages.title: Snowbird (song)
pages.extract:
"Snowbird" is a song written by Canadian singer-songwriter Gene MacLellan. Though it has been recorded by many performers, it is best known through Anne Murray's 1969 recording. "Snowbird" appeared as a track in mid-1969 on Murray's second studio album This Way Is My Way, and was released in mid-1970 as a single. 
The song was a No. 2 hit on Canada's pop chart and went to No. 1 on both the Canadian adult contemporary and country charts. The song reached No. 8 on the U.S. pop singles chart, spent six weeks at No. 1 on the U.S. adult contemporary chart, and became a surprise Top 10 U.S. country hit as well. It was certified as a gold single by the RIAA, the first American Gold record ever awarded to a Canadian solo female artist. It peaked at No. 23 on the UK Singles Chart. In 2003 it was an inaugural song inductee of the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame.
Anne Murray and Gene MacLellan had met while both were regulars on the CBC television series Singalong Jubilee and Murray recorded two of MacLellan's compositions, "Snowbird" and "Biding My Time", for her first major label album release, This Way Is My Way, in 1969. Murray would recall: "Gene told me he wrote ["Snowbird"] in twenty minutes while walking on a beach on Prince Edward Island."
"Snowbird" sold well over a million copies and was picked as 19th on the 50 Tracks: The Canadian Version list, a partially populist approach to defining the most influential songs by Canadians.

"'''Snowbird'''" is a song written by Canadian singer-songwriter [[Gene MacLellan]]. Though it has been recorded by many performers, it is best known through [[Anne Murray]]'s 1969 recording. "Snowbird" appeared as a track in mid-1969 on Murray's second studio album ''[[This Way Is My Way]]'',<ref>{{Citation |title=Anne Murray - This Way Is My Way |date=1969 |url=https://www.discogs.com/master/751286-Anne-Murray-This-Way-Is-My-Way |access-date=2025-10-13 |language=en}}</ref> and was released in mid-1970 as a single.<ref>{{Citation |title=Anne Murray - Snowbird |date=1970 |url=https://www.discogs.com/release/4387626-Anne-Murray-Snowbird |access-date=2025-10-13 |language=en}}</ref> 

The song was a No. 2 hit on Canada's pop chart and went to No. 1 on both the Canadian adult contemporary and country charts. The song reached No. 8 on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|pop singles chart]], spent six weeks at No. 1 on the U.S. [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|adult contemporary chart]], and became a surprise Top 10 U.S. [[Hot Country Songs|country hit]] as well. It was certified as a gold single by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]], the first American Gold record ever awarded to a Canadian solo female artist.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720082807/http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&action=&title=Snowbird&artist=&format=SINGLE&debutLP=&category=&sex=&releaseDate=&requestNo=&type=&level=&label=&company=&certificationDate=&awardDescription=&catalogNo=&aSex=&rec_id=&charField=&gold=&platinum=&multiPlat=&level2=&certDate=&album=&id=&after=&before=&startMonth=1&endMonth=1&startYear=1958&endYear=2009&sort=Artist&perPage=25|url-status=dead|title=RIAA - Recording Industry Association of America|website = [[Recording Industry Association of America]]|archive-date = July 20, 2012}}</ref> It peaked at No. 23 on the [[UK Singles Chart]]. In 2003 it was an inaugural song inductee of the [[Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.songfacts.com/detail.php?id=2319 |title=Snowbird by Anne Murray Songfacts |website=Songfacts.com |access-date=October 3, 2016}}</ref>

Anne Murray and Gene MacLellan had met while both were regulars on the [[CBC Television|CBC television]] series ''[[Singalong Jubilee]]'' and Murray recorded two of MacLellan's compositions, "Snowbird" and "Biding My Time", for her first major label album release, ''This Way Is My Way'', in 1969. Murray would recall: "Gene told me he wrote ["Snowbird"] in twenty minutes while walking on a beach on [[Prince Edward Island]]."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genemaclellan.com/?page_id=27 |title=Bio |publisher=Gene MacLellan |access-date=October 3, 2016}}</ref>

"Snowbird" sold well over a million copies<ref>{{Cite news |last=Marten |first=Suzanne |date=August 28, 1986 |title=Murray Thrills 5,000 at Fair |pages=27 |work=The Post-Standard {{!}} Syracuse Post Standard |url=https://www.newspaperarchive.com/us/new-york/syracuse/syracuse-post-standard/1986/08-28/page-27/ |access-date=July 26, 2022}}</ref> and was picked as 19th on the ''[[50 Tracks: The Canadian Version]]'' list, a partially populist approach to defining the most influential songs by Canadians.
